audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3].side and phases[5].side read 'Skill' and phases[6].side read 'Kassadin', while content win[0..6] and the packet levelChart both read Katarina on all seven rows.
audit.why: Cross-layer disagreement. The full-layer whys on those rows already describe Katarina winning, and the content whys[6] states 'You-favoured ... but only barely'. 50.52% over 2718 games is a narrow Katarina edge, which is the row verdict already recorded in the content layer.
audit.corrected: phases[3].side, phases[5].side and phases[6].side set to Katarina to match win[3], win[5], win[6] and the packet chart. Whys unchanged because they already argue the Katarina side.

audit.why: Correctly recorded: Katarina bullies pre-6, level 6 turns from kill-lane to deny-lane because Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3, first item outruns Rod of Ages, and his stacking Riftwalk is the late-game clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in the matchup was nowhere on the page: Null Sphere's Riot text says it deals damage 'and interrupting channels' — it cancels Death Lotus. The page instead framed Riftwalk as the tracked ability. breakdown.cooldowns also had no digit in it, dosFull[2].d claimed a 'fifteen-second invitation' with no source, and two bullet bodies were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles.
audit.why: Katarina's R carries the 'channel: interruptible — any CC cancels it' flag and Kassadin's Q explicitly interrupts channels on a 9s rank-1 cooldown. That, not Riftwalk, is what decides whether a committed fight works.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now leads with Null Sphere at 9s interrupting channels, gives Riftwalk 5s to 2s and Force Pulse 21s; dosFull[2].d, tradeBad and breakdown.trading now state the interrupt; the unsourced 'fifteen-second' magnitude is gone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The brief's missingInteractions entry — Kassadin's combo opening with the Nether Blade auto-attack reset, so the wind-up rather than the spell cast is the cue to step back — was absent from every field.
audit.why: Nether Blade carries the autoReset flag and is a flat 7s cooldown, so the tell arrives before any spell animation does.
50.52% over 2718 games, already on the page in the late field.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E Shunpo (second use) like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.

edits.after: Q the bounce, E to the landed dagger, W as you spin out — trade whenever Null Sphere's 9s is down.

edits.after: Shunpo in with Null Sphere up — he interrupts the Lotus, Force Pulse slows the exit, and Riftwalk leaves you standing there.

edits.before: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Riftwalk costs 40 mana and stacks up fast — in a 2v2 he escapes but leaves his partner to your resets.

edits.before: Q the bounce, E to the landed dagger, W as you spin out — steel-routed trades his aim can't follow.
edits.after: Shunpo reaches 725 and costs no mana — enter on a landed dagger and keep the second use as the exit.

edits.before: Kassadin burns Riftwalk on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Null Sphere interrupts channels on a 9s cooldown — Lotus only once he has spent it.

edits.before: That’s Kassadin’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: His Q shield absorbs magic damage and Riftwalk exits — bring a jungler, not a coin.

edits.before: Your lotus dies to one interrupt — counting their CC before spinning is the entire skill floor of the champion.
edits.after: Shunpo is 12s at rank 1; spend both uses going in and Riftwalk leaves you alone in his wave.

edits.before: Shunpo onto a face with the CC still loaded — Katarina dies to held buttons, not skill, and everyone holding one knows it.
edits.after: Away from your daggers there are no resets and no exit — the Nether Blade auto plus a Force Pulse slow ends the trade.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to 6 behind the Null Sphere shield, then using Riftwalk to leave every fight you start.

edits.before: Ahead, chain it: zone Kassadin off daggers, lotus every skirmish, and reset through the map — fed Katarina is a weather event.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the scaling: shove him in, take plates, and roam — every minute he farms is Riftwalk stacks you cannot outrun.

edits.before: Carry through chain reactions — one kill is three; your job is the first domino and the discipline to wait for it.
edits.after: Carry by ending it early — kill him while Riftwalk is still 5s, and the reset chain does the rest of the game.

edits.before: Dagger geometry and patience — chip the no-CC kits, bait the CC ones, and bank patterns for the 6 that changes the lane's species.
edits.after: Bully him: pre-6 he has no escape, the Null Sphere shield eats one dagger tick, and every denied minion pushes Rod of Ages later.

edits.before: First item onward, hunt skirmishes: every 2v2 near your daggers is a reset chain waiting for a signature. Roam when mid stalls.
edits.after: His combo opens with a Nether Blade auto reset — the wind-up, not the spell cast, is your cue to step back. Roam when mid stalls.

edits.before: You are the cleanup that starts fights: enter on steel, lotus the clump, reset through the kill, and exit through the panic.
edits.after: Shunpo him the instant he Riftwalks onto your carry — that is the one moment he stands still inside your dagger range.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-bounced thin push with daggers banked at the river mouth — your roams arrive with luggage. Worst wave: a frozen wave near a CC mage's tower — every pickup walk is a stun audition. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.
edits.after: Best wave: shoved onto him pre-6, when he has no escape and every missed minion delays Rod of Ages. Worst wave: a frozen wave he clears with Force Pulse while you walk up into Nether Blade range. Crash timing: crash and roam — Riftwalk defends one lane and he cannot cover two.
